approaches.name: AI-assisted airborne geophysics and digital drill core data for mineral prospectivity mapping
approaches.description: The project uses airborne geophysical surveys, sensor-scanned drill cores and AI/ML predictive models to map and rank mineral exploration targets. Practices: High-resolution airborne geophysics and prospectivity mapping datasets; Mineral systems approach for national geological prospectivity mapping; Sensor-scanned digitization of national drill core collections; AI/ML-assisted mineral prospectivity mapping from airborne surveys; groundwater resource assessments and geological hazard mapping feeding territorial planning and mining screening; probabilistic geoscience mapping products to prioritize exploration targets; Predictive modeling and airborne surveys to de-risk exploration; Digital drill core library database for geological samples; Airborne geophysical and remote-sensing mineral datasets.

evidence.text: High-resolution airborne geophysics and surface mapping datasets published and accessible (km²).

extra_evidence.text: Target: 310,698 km² airborne (≤500 m spacing);

128,645 km² airborne (≤250 m, covering 24 smaller selection or targeted blocks); these 128,645 km² will include detailed geochemistry, field geological mapping validation and final prospectivity mapping (probabilities of exploration success) at higher-resolution scales of 1:50,000.

This investment represents a strategic innovation in Peru’s mining sector, moving from conventional geological mapping toward a modern mineral systems approach that strengthens national geoscience capacity and supports diversification into critical minerals.

With World Bank support, INGEMMET and the Government will gain the tools and methodologies to build a stronger, investors´ oriented and more resilient geological knowledge infrastructure—placing Peru closer to the global leaders in geological prospectivity mapping, alongside Australia, Canada, and the United States.

The establishment of a national drill core library will allow for systematic preservation, cataloging, digitization and sensor-scanning of geological evidence accumulated over decades, including drill cores, samples, and associated technical documentation and scanned images (from visible, infrared and multispectral sensors).

Existing collections—comprising approximately 60,000 meters of drill cores and 77,000 geological samples are dispersed across various locations/ facilities and stored under inadequate conditions, limiting their preservation and hindering access to critical data for exploration and research, with drill cores forming the highest value part of an exploration survey.

The new datasets will be processed and interpreted using advanced methodologies such as mineral systems analysis, predictive modeling, and AI-assisted Machine Learning techniques, thereby enhancing mineral prospectivity (probabilities of exploration success) and fostering a more efficient and sustainable mining sector.
Airborne geophysical surveys (magnetic and gravimetric) will be carried out over a total area of 310,698 km².

The Project will also use groundwater resource assessments and geological hazard mapping to support climate-informed territorial planning, early screening of mining proposals, and disaster risk management.
As a result, the geoscience mapping program will deliver not only modern, high-resolution maps but also probabilistic mapping products that help identify and prioritize exploration targets.
These targets, once selected, can advance toward potential mineral “discoveries” through subsequent detailed investment and exploration work.
The project aims to de-risk exploration through high-resolution airborne surveys, predictive modeling, and regulatory modernization.
This indicator reflects the increase in private investment in mining Description exploration, catalyzed by improved geoscientific data and streamlined permitting.
It will be equipped with Description advanced storage systems, radiometric scanning equipment, and a digital database to ensure public and private sector access.

The facility will house existing and future drill core samples, geological specimens, and historical exploration records.

Frequency Annual Data source INGEMMET lab reports Methodology for Data Review of reports Collection Responsibility for Data INGEMMET Collection Intermediate Results Indicator 1.3: Number of new geological, geochemical, or geophysical datasets produced This indicator measures the number of new datasets generated through airborne geophysical surveys, geochemical sampling, and remote sensing.
These analyses support predictive targeting and mineral systems mapping.
These datasets enhance Peru’s mineral prospectivity assessments and reduce geological Description uncertainty.

approaches.name: Interoperable digital one-stop shop for mining permitting
approaches.description: The project builds a transactional VUD platform interlinking over ten permitting entities, automating workflows and integrating water, environmental and consultation data. Practices: Ventanilla Única Digital (VUD) online mining permitting platform; Interinstitutional Mining Digital One-Stop Shop (VUD) for permits; Interoperable automated workflow platform for MINEM regulatory processes; Interoperable digital one-stop shop for mining permits (VUD MINEM); Interoperable permitting platform linking permits, water and consultation modules; Fully transactional VUD-MINEM platform scaling piloted informative tool; Interoperable digital platforms integrating water authorizations, environmental information and socio-environmental commitments into permitting and oversight; VUD digital one-stop shop for mining permits; Digitalization and integration of core MINEM permitting workflows into centralized platforms; VUD one-stop shop consolidating mining permit steps.
approaches.why_innovative: New delivery arrangement: single digital window for mining permits - cue: 'digital transformation of' | category Operational; adoption apply; judged in 2 round(s); context expanded; final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The digital transformation of the MINEM is essential to operationalize an effective Ventanilla Única Digital (VUD) that streamlines permitting, reduces uncertainty, and restores investor confidence.

extra_evidence.text: This component will strengthen MINEM’s capacity to lead sectoral modernization through three integrated interventions: (i) the digital transformation of its regulatory and administrative processes, (ii) the implementation of an interinstitutional Mining Digital One-Stop Shop VUD to centralize and streamline authorization procedures from exploration through mine closure, and (iii) the establishment of Technical Training Centers for ASM to improve skills, productivity, and compliance.

Designed as a coherent package, these measures will equip MINEM and partner agencies with modern tools, efficient workflows, and specialized services that work in concert to reduce permitting times, strengthen oversight and territorial coordination, and expand technical training for ASM miners.

Building on the identified gaps, the subcomponent will digitalize core administrative and regulatory procedures, integrate dispersed information into interoperable platforms, and establish standardized, automated workflows to ensure consistent and transparent 7 This subcomponent corresponds to Improvement of geochronology research services in the district of San Borja, Province of Lima, Department of Lima from the client’s public investment system [invierte.pe] 8 This subcomponent corresponds to Improvement and expansion of operational or institutional mission services in the information systems of the Ministry of Energy and Mines, District of San Borja, province of Lima, Lima department from the client’s public investment system [invierte.pe] Page 10 application of regulations.
Core administrative processes remain fragmented, with procedures still largely paper-based and inconsistently applied, while critical information is dispersed across non-interoperable systems.

The VUD MINEM will address these challenges by facilitating the interoperability of all procedures—from exploration to mine closure—into a single digital transaction platform led by MINEM as the authority, strengthening transparency, traceability, and predictability.
Subcomponent 2.2: Development of the digital one-stop shop for mining permits (VUD MINEM).
The absence of interoperability across environmental, social, and technical agencies has been identified as a major bottleneck undermining sector competitiveness.

This subcomponent will finance the design, development, piloting, and implementation of an interoperable platform that connects all relevant permitting entities, enabling real-time process management and integrated oversight.

The VUD MINEM will incorporate modules to interlink transactions in real time for mining permits, water use authorizations, and prior consultation with Indigenous Peoples, while also recording and tracking socio-environmental commitments.

The VUD will streamline procedures, reduce permitting times, strengthen regulatory predictability and oversight, while each participating entity will continue to exercise its own competencies and mandates, and integrate technical data to support evidence-based decision-making.
On the regulatory side, MINEM has piloted the first phase of the VUD-MINEM platform as an informative digital tool, which has already demonstrated the potential to improve transparency.

The project will build on this foundation by developing and operating a fully transactional VUD, aimed at streamlining procedures, reducing permitting times, and strengthening regulatory predictability and oversight.

By integrating water use authorizations, environmental information, and socio-environmental commitments into interoperable digital platforms, the Project strengthens the capacity of public institutions to systematically incorporate climate and water risks into permitting, monitoring, and oversight processes.
The VUD platform integrates multiple government agencies into a single digital interface, Description enabling real-time tracking, automated workflows, and transparent decision-making.

The goal is to improve efficiency, transparency, and service delivery.
